Where to record a deed and office hours

Any deed for Shelby County land gets recorded through the Register of Deeds. Go to the main office at 1075 Mullins Station Road, Building W-3, Memphis, TN 38134 (mail goes to Suite W165). The register's website lists weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. You can call 901-222-8100.

Downtown Memphis and Southbrook have counters too. Look at the home page before you drive over, because a temporary closure may send in-person filers to a drop box at Mullins Station. The office takes cash, cashier's checks, money orders, business checks and most major credit cards.

Clerks only record. Drafting help and legal advice are off the table, and there is no public notary on site. Get the deed signed in front of a notary beforehand, which many banks offer.

Walking in with a complete package saves a second trip. Bring the signed and notarized original, a copy of your prior deed, the parcel number, and payment that covers the recording fee and any tax. If a title company is handling your sale, ask it to send the deed for you and confirm the date it expects the recorded copy back, since that date is when the new owner shows up in the public record.

Items a deed must include

Filing guidelines spell out what a taxable deed needs, citing a Tennessee Code section for each. Leaving one out can get the deed rejected, which is why title companies and attorneys run through this list. The main items:

  • Names of the grantor and grantee, plus a proper acknowledgment (T.C.A. 66-22-101)
  • Affidavit of value, required if the deed is taxable (67-4-409)
  • Derivation clause that cites the previous recorded deed (66-24-110)
  • Street address of the property, except for vacant land (66-24-113)
  • Owner's name and address, and the same for the party paying property tax (66-24-114)
  • Ward, block and parcel numbers (66-24-122)
  • Preparer's name and address (66-24-115)
  • Legal description, with a signed original unless the filing is electronic

A deed that clears the minimum legal requirements with fees paid is recorded and mailed back in about a business day, and a digital image is posted online.

What a deed costs to file

Filing a sale deed costs a recording fee and the state realty transfer tax. Recording runs $12.00 for two pages or fewer, made up of a $10.00 page fee and a $2.00 fee the guidelines itemize, with $5.00 for each extra page. Tax is $0.37 per $100 of whichever is greater, price or value, and $1.00 more is added when state tax is collected. Quitclaim deeds differ because their tax rests only on the consideration actually given.

Shelby County recording charges
Document or serviceCharge
Warranty or quitclaim deed, up to 2 pages$12.00
Each added page$5.00
Realty transfer tax$0.37 per $100
Mortgage tax$0.115 per $100, first $2,000 exempt
Certified copy$1.00 per page
Plain copy at the counter$0.50 per page ($1.50 for plats)

Refunds of overpaid transfer or mortgage tax come from the Tennessee Department of Revenue rather than the register. Send copies of the instruments, the tax receipts, a brief explanation and a claim form, along with a Report of Debt form if the refund is over $200.

Transfers that owe no transfer tax

Some transfers owe no realty transfer tax and need no oath of value. Ones a family is likely to meet when retitling a house:

  • Spouse-to-spouse deeds that create or end a tenancy by the entirety
  • Executor's deed that carries out a will
  • Divorce decree or deed that adjusts rights between the former spouses
  • Moves into or out of a revocable living trust by the same owner or a spouse
  • Trustee's deed handing real estate to the beneficiaries

A normal sale to an unrelated buyer is taxable. Unsure which category yours falls into? Put the question to your closing attorney before signing.

Can a seller e-file?

Private individuals cannot e-file here. A state law in effect since July 1, 2025 (T.C.A. 47-10-118) restricts electronic filing to attorneys, banks, credit unions, federally backed and regulated lenders, title insurers and agents, and government bodies, and every e-filed document needs an electronic certification form under T.C.A. 66-24-101.

Opening an e-filing account may take 48 hours or more, so sellers normally lean on the title company's account. Heavy filers can set up an escrow account that draws shortages and credits overages on its own. Send account forms to 1075 Mullins Station Road, W-165, Memphis, TN 38134.

Owners may also sign up for the Property Fraud Alert program, which warns them when something threatens their title.

After a death or a loan payoff

Families of a deceased owner are sent to the Shelby County Probate Court Clerk, 901-222-3750, to find out whether a will went through probate. A probated will may stand in for the deed. Without one, an Affidavit of Heirship is recorded for $10.00 on the first two pages plus the $2.00 fee, and title companies generally ask for three affidavits from three witnesses, two of them outside the family.

Paying off a loan produces a trust deed release, and the register can find it for you. The office does not do lien searches, since certain liens live in court files and not in the land records.

Recording and your property tax bill

A recorded deed transfers title but leaves the tax bill untouched. Before closing, ask the Shelby County Trustee where the current and any past-due bills stand, and ask the Assessor of Property how your parcel is valued. The county Board of Equalization opens appeals May 1, a month ahead of most Tennessee counties, so an appeal here has an earlier deadline.

Closings run in a fixed order. First the deed is drafted and its legal description compared with the prior deed. Next you sign before a notary and the tax payoff is paid. Your attorney or the title company then submits the deed, and the register records and returns it. Because the register cannot advise or help with forms, raise any oddity with your closing attorney before signing. A cash sale follows the same path without a lender's mortgage documents to record, and it keeps the paper trail short.

Frequently asked questions

How long does Shelby County take to record a deed?

Roughly one business day. The deed is recorded and mailed back in about that time, and a digital copy appears on the website.

Can I record my own deed online in Shelby County?

Not as an individual. State law confines electronic submission to attorneys, banks, lenders, title companies and government bodies. Go through a title company or attorney that has an account, or mail or hand-deliver the original.

What does recording a quitclaim deed cost in Shelby County?

Expect about $12 for up to two pages. If any tax is due, it is figured only on the consideration given, at $0.37 per $100.

Does the Shelby County register help fill out deeds?

No. Staff only record documents, and they cannot advise you or fill in forms. No notary is available to the public, so get the signature notarized before you arrive.

How do I get a copy of my Shelby County deed?

Start on the register's website, where many recorded documents can be viewed and copied free. If yours is not there, ask in person, by email or by mail and supply names, a date or the property address. Copies at the counter are $0.50 a page.

Office location and what it does

You will find the Register of Deeds in the City-County Building, 400 Main Street, Suite 225, Knoxville, TN 37902. The main number is 865-215-2330, and records staff answer at 865-215-2329. Weekday counter hours are eight to half past four. The office website describes it as a recording agency only. It files deeds, deeds of trust, liens, lien releases, powers of attorney, bonds and plats. Staff cannot write your deed or give legal advice, so plan to use your closing attorney or title company for anything beyond filing. Call 865-215-2329 with questions about the process itself.

Only land inside Knox County can be recorded here, and a deed for a house in a neighboring county will be sent back. Handwritten records reach back to the late 1700s. Every record is public except military discharges.

To search, start with an owner's name, a legal description and a rough recording date. Clear title still needs a title company or abstractor to confirm it, because liens, easements and court judgments are not all filed in this office.

Recording fees and transfer taxes

Tennessee statute sets the recording fees, which appear on the county's fee schedule. For a warranty, quitclaim or trust deed, the first two pages cost $12.00 and each extra page costs $5.00. Add $1.00 for taxable documents. Certified copies are $1.00 a page. An online fee calculator lets you estimate the total before filing.

Transfer tax is charged on the value of the sale. Mortgage tax applies to a deed of trust once the exempt first portion is set aside. The closing agent will give you the exact totals for your transaction.

What a deed needs to be accepted

A filing requirements page spells out what warranty, quitclaim and trustee's deeds need. Most delays come from a missing item, so walk through these points before the deed leaves the closing table:

  • The land lies in Knox County, and the preparer's name and complete address are on the deed
  • Seller signatures are notarized, and an original is presented
  • The buyer's name and address appear, along with the responsible taxpayer
  • Value and consideration are stated, and the value is taxable
  • The prior deed is cited by instrument number or by book and page, and a legal description is included

A warranty deed can show $0.00 consideration only between spouses, for an exempt entity, or when property moves into a revocable living trust. A trustee's deed or substitute trustee's deed must carry a trust deed reference and an appointment reference. Other reasons for rejection include names too faint to index, a copied notary seal, a missing exhibit, or a missing chain of title.

Bring photo identification to the signing and sign in front of the notary, not before. Notarization is the preferred method, though two witnesses can also work. Plats are accepted in two sizes only: 24 by 36 inches and 18 by 24 inches.

Recording time and deadlines

Most filings are recorded the same day they arrive. Staff checks that the document is recordable and the fees are right, assigns an instrument number, scans it, indexes it and verifies the data, which usually takes a day. The original then goes back to the filer. Tennessee sets no time limit for recording a deed, but the office recommends doing it quickly, since an unrecorded deed invites legal trouble.

The website offers e-recording, a request form for deed copies and a lien release form. After a mortgage is paid off, the lender files a release with the register, and you can get a copy from the office. If you lose your deed, the recording is the primary evidence of ownership, and a certified copy works as the original.

A change in ownership generally requires a new deed recorded here. The exceptions are court cases such as probate, divorce or foreclosure, and certain deaths where the right language exists and a death certificate is recorded. Adding or removing a name also takes a newly prepared deed, and the office suggests an attorney or title company prepare it.

Fraud alerts and public reports

Property fraud is a real risk in county records, so the office runs a free Fraud Notification System at alertme.knoxrod.org. Owners enter their names and get an email whenever a document under a matching name is recorded.

The office also publishes reports that help a seller price and time a sale:

  • A weekly real estate transfers report, sortable by value, with an email signup
  • Reports on money borrowed against real estate and taxes collected on mortgage records and transfers
  • A top lenders report showing every lender, the amount loaned and the number of loans in Knox County
  • Historic tax maps from the 1950s and 1980s, plus a legacy deed search

Military discharge papers (DD214s) can be recorded here at no fee, and those records stay confidential.

Where this office fits in a sale

In Knox County, a sale finishes at this office. Deed, transfer tax and recording fee all go here, and the staff recommends having an attorney or title company prepare the deed. Ask your closing agent who will file it and when. After recording, the Property Assessor changes the owner's name, which can take as long as a week.

For a seller the sequence looks like this: the title company prepares the deed, you sign before a notary, the closing agent submits it with the fees, and the office assigns an instrument number once it is indexed. Keep the certified copy for your records, since it works as the original. If you are selling an inherited house, check that the deed that put the estate's name or your name on the property is itself recorded, because the new deed refers back to it by instrument number or book and page. A missing link in that chain is a common reason a deed comes back unrecorded.

Before closing, ask the Trustee about any unpaid county tax so it can be cleared at the table. Locally, the county had 232,546 housing units and 5,013 building permits in 2025, so this office handles a steady stream of deeds and mortgage releases. For a house with a cloudy history, such as an inherited property, a title company can trace the recorded chain and tell you what needs fixing before the deed is signed.

Frequently asked questions

What do Knox County deed filings cost?

The base charge is $12.00 for a deed of up to two pages, then $5.00 for every extra page, plus $1.00 on taxable documents. The property transfer tax is $0.37 for each $100 of value.

Does a Knox County deed have to be notarized?

Yes. Seller signatures must be notarized, or witnessed by two people, and the original has to be presented. A notary is the preferred method.

Does Tennessee set a deadline for recording a deed in Knox County?

No. Tennessee sets no time limit, but the Register of Deeds recommends recording as soon as possible after the sale to avoid legal problems.

Can a deed carry no sale price?

Only in limited cases. A warranty deed can show $0.00 consideration between spouses, for an exempt entity, or when property is moved into a revocable living trust.

Office address and role

The Blount County Register of Deeds is at 349 Court Street, Maryville, TN 37804. The phone number is 865-273-5880, and the doors are open weekdays from 8 a.m. until 4:30 p.m.

The office works like a filing counter. The staff will not search a title, hand you forms or draft a document. Sellers in Blount County usually get the deed from a title company or real estate attorney, and the register files it after the tax has been paid.

The seat of the county, and its biggest city, is Maryville. Alcoa, Friendsville, Rockford and Townsend are cities as well, and Louisville is a town. Tennessee records land county by county, so all of these addresses are handled at the same Court Street counter.

Before closing day, ask the title company whether it will e-record or deliver a paper original. A paper deed needs the fees paid up front and an envelope if you want the original sent back, while e-recording goes through one of the approved vendors. Either way, ask for the recording information afterward and keep it with your sale papers, since you will need the book and page reference if the deed is ever referred to again.

Local market in brief

As of July 2025, an estimated 143,820 people live in Blount County, in 64,682 housing units. Owners occupy 77.0 percent of those units, and a typical owner-occupied house was valued at $320,500 across 2020 to 2024. Public schools are run by Blount County Schools, except in Maryville and Alcoa, which have their own systems. School district, city limits and proximity to park land all vary by address, so confirm the parcel's jurisdiction before you list. Write down the district, map and parcel number now, because the deed will need them and they are quicker to find on a tax bill than in a rush at closing.

Recording fees

Recording a document of one or two pages is $12. Every additional page or attachment adds $5, and any document with a taxable amount, like a warranty deed or deed of trust, also gets a $1 clerk fee.

Document or serviceCounty fee
Recording, one or two pages$12

You pay fees when you file. The counter accepts cash, checks, credit or debit cards and money orders. Because page count drives the fee, have the register confirm the total in advance whenever your deed comes with attachments.

Transfer tax on a home sale

Under Tennessee law each $100 of the price, or of the value if higher, carries $0.37 in tax. Legally the buyer named as grantee owes it, and the register takes payment as the deed is filed.

When the buyer finances, a mortgage tax applies too, at $0.115 per $100 for everything borrowed past the first $2,000. Purchase agreements sometimes shift these costs, so look at yours.

In front of the register, the grantee swears on the deed's face to the real consideration or the value, taking the larger number. Lying about value can be prosecuted as perjury. State reviewers also line deed values up against assessor values, and a suspiciously low price can bring an inquiry letter.

What a deed must include

Expect the counter to reject a deed that lacks any of these county requirements.

  • A Prepared By line, with name and address, on each document.
  • District, map and parcel number, plus name and address for both the owner and the responsible taxpayer.
  • Book and page references in a format such as WD508 Pg 61. The office cannot reference documents by instrument number.
  • On trust deeds, mortgages, modifications and assignments, the sentence: 'Maximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes is $____.' Even a zero amount must be written.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope if you want the original returned, which the office does for real estate documents after recording.

A recorded error cannot be corrected by hand. Recording the document again needs new signatures and a notary, unless you file a scrivener's error affidavit that refers to the earlier document and states the correction. If the owner is wrong, a new deed must be prepared and filed.

Exempt transfers

The state recordation tax manual names transfers that owe no realty transfer tax. Several are common in family and estate sales, and none needs an oath of consideration.

  • Transfers of a leasehold.
  • A spouse conveying to the other to create or end a tenancy by the entirety.
  • An executor's deed carrying out a devise in a will.
  • Divorce decrees and deeds that settle property between the spouses.
  • Moves into or out of a revocable living trust by the same person or spouse.
  • Transfers with a government body.

Quitclaim deeds are taxed on the consideration given. But if the language, such as 'in fee simple' or 'to have and to hold', shows the grantor meant to convey the property itself, fair market value is the base. Ask the title agent which way yours will be read.

Searching and e-recording

Deed records are not on the county website. Public computers at 349 Court Street let you search in person. Online access runs through a vendor, US Title Search Network (ustitlesearch.net, 615-223-1823), and you contact that company to subscribe.

E-recording comes in through Simplifile (800-460-5657) or CSC (1-866-403-5272). Copies cost $0.50 to email each document or $0.50 per page to print. Certified copies that serve as an original are $1.00 per page. An independent service called CRS (Courthouse Retrieval) is not run by the county or the register, so errors in its data go to that company.

The register does not track foreclosure sales posted on the courthouse steps. When a lender sale is pending on your house, the lender or its trustee has the schedule. A title agency can verify what is recorded on the parcel.

Getting a Blount County sale to the register

The sequence is brief. Your title company or attorney drafts the deed, including the parcel number and addresses described above. The buyer takes the oath of value, and tax and fees are paid on recording. Payoffs and old liens get cleared by the title company beforehand.

A house that needs repairs, or one tied up in an unfinished estate, can be sold to us as-is. We pay cash for Blount County houses, and the deed still goes through this office under identical rules. Gather the previous deed, your tax bill and payoff figures first.

How do I reach the Blount County Register of Deeds?

The line is 865-273-5880. Visit 349 Court Street, Maryville, TN 37804 on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.

What will recording my deed cost in Blount County?

The fee is $12 for up to two pages and $5 per page beyond that. Documents with a taxable amount pick up a $1 clerk fee, and a sale adds the $0.37 per $100 transfer tax.

On a house sale, who owes the Tennessee transfer tax?

The buyer named on the deed is the one who owes it under the statute, although your contract may divide the cost differently.

Can I look up Blount County deeds online?

Only through a vendor. Searchers are sent to ustitlesearch.net, which needs a subscription. Free computers are available at 349 Court Street.

Will the register write my deed or search my title?

No. It only records. Hire a title company or attorney for drafting the deed and searching the title.

  • Parcel number, plus a sworn statement of value if the deed is taxable

After recording, the document is scanned into the database for online viewing. Store the recorded copy with your closing papers, as lenders and buyers sometimes ask later for its instrument number. Spot a misspelled name or a wrong parcel number? Report it to your closing agent promptly so a correcting document can be prepared and recorded.

Step by step for a seller

A typical sale moves through this office in a few moves. The deed is prepared by your title company or attorney and checked against the list above, then you sign in front of a notary. The original reaches the register by e-recording or on paper at Suite 201, and staff index it, take the tax and fees, and enter it in the database.

Recording fees are small compared with the tax. If the house came to you through a will or a divorce, ask whether the transfer is one of the exempt types before the deed is drawn, since that changes what your closing agent must collect.

When in doubt that a document can be recorded as written, call 615-452-3892 before mailing. A question costs less than a returned packet. Mailed packets should include the original deed, a check or money order that covers recording and tax, and a note with your phone number so staff can reach you about a missing item. Is the house really in Sumner County?

Not always. Goodlettsville partly lies in Davidson County, and Millersville, Portland and White House each stretch into Robertson County. A Sumner city name on the mail therefore says little about the parcel's county. Verify with the Assessor's property search or the parcel number on the deed before choosing a register, and ask the title company where the filing goes.

Recording puts a new name on the record but pays no tax. The county bill is due the first Monday in October and goes delinquent after February 28. Call the Trustee, 615-452-1260, for the parcel balance before you close, and give the Assessor, 615-452-2412, the new owner's mailing address.

Agree on the order of events with your closing agent. Balance first, then signing and notarizing, then filing, then the scan appearing in the database. With a cash buyer there is no deed of trust and no mortgage tax, so the packet is shorter.

Certified records start in September 1989 and are searchable online, and digitized deed books and indexes reach back to 1786.

$0.37 for each $100 of purchase price, paid at recording. Your title company can compute the exact amount for your deal.

A home sale tends to involve several counters, and the courthouse keeps them close together. The Property Assessor is in Suite 210 West, the Trustee in Room 212W, the Clerk and Master in Suite 108 W, and the County Clerk in Suite 202E. You can get a deed recorded, a tax payoff and an ownership update done in a single trip. Mailed documents are accepted too.

If you come in person, bring the signed original, payment for the fee and taxes, and the prior deed for reference. Staff can tell you at the counter whether the page count and the required statements are in order before the document is accepted.

What the office records

Any paper the law says may be recorded against real estate comes through this office, which indexes and stores it under statutory rules. For a seller, that boils down to deeds, deeds of trust, mortgages, amendments, assignments and releases. Staff also log every fee, commission and tax the office takes in.

Every recorded paper gets a book and page citation, such as T508 Pg 61 or Bk 1411 Pg 32. Title examiners follow those citations backward through each prior owner. Land records are searchable through the link on the county's Register of Deeds page. After recording, the Assessor reads the deed, changes the owner on the tax maps, and the following bill goes to the new owner.

Sevier County was formed in 1794 and has kept its original boundaries, so the chain of title for an older farm or mountain tract stays in one set of land books. A parcel near the county line may still need a look at the neighboring county's records for easements or older surveys. Ask a title examiner which indexes to search before you list.

Recording fees and taxes

Recording a deed, deed of trust or mortgage that runs two pages or fewer is a flat $12.00, and a price-based tax comes on top. Amendments, modifications, assignments and releases are also $12.00 for two pages.

Who pays the transfer tax

Payment falls on the buyer, who is the grantee in the deed. Tennessee's recordation tax comes in two pieces: a realty transfer tax on moving title, and a mortgage tax on documents that secure debt. Both are collected at the Register's counter and sent on to the state.

The transfer tax applies to most transfers, with some exceptions, since the buyer is the party asking for the deed to be placed on record. Mortgage tax falls on the borrower. A financed purchase therefore shows two separate taxes at recording, one on the price and one on the loan. Your purchase contract decides how each is assigned, and the settlement statement shows the result.

Recording documents by mail

Send the document, plus a stamped envelope bearing your own address, to the Sevier County Register of Deeds, 125 Court Avenue, Suite 209W, Sevierville, TN 37862. Originals are always returned after recording, and the envelope lets the office send them back promptly. Run through this list before sealing the packet:

  • Enclose payment for the recording fee and any taxes that apply.

  • Confirm the legal description and parties match the prior deed in the chain of title.

Unsure about one particular instrument? Phone 865.453.2758 first, then mail.

Protecting yourself from deed fraud

The office offers a name alert. Register a name or business, and the Register notifies you if a document is filed under it, so you can spot and stop a fraudulent transaction right away. As of March 3, 2025, the property fraud and online records links moved to new web addresses, so use the links on the county page rather than old bookmarks.

The alert suits owners of vacation cabins, inherited houses and vacant parcels that nobody watches day to day. Those are exactly the properties where an unexpected filing is easy to miss. If an alert ever arrives for a document you did not sign, call the Register at 865.453.2758 right away and ask what was filed, then bring in your own deed so staff can compare the two.

Other steps when selling a Sevier County house

Recording comes last in a closing, and clearing taxes comes first. The Trustee in Room 212W bills the owner of record and accepts partial payments. Payment opens October 1 and stays penalty free until the end of February, after which 1.5 percent monthly interest applies. A delinquent account goes to the Clerk and Master, and after a tax sale the owner has one year to redeem.

The Assessor in Suite 210 West uses January 1 as the assessment date and updates ownership from recorded deeds. Before closing, work through these items:

  • Give the closing agent a copy of your current deed.
  • Ask the Register's office about any unusual instrument before you sign.
  • Pull your deed from the land records and compare the legal description with your contract.

The order of events is short. The closing agent gathers the signed deed and the taxes, the Register records the deed, and the Assessor then redirects the tax bill to the buyer. A cash sale follows the same path but skips the lender's mortgage paperwork, so no mortgage tax is recorded unless the buyer borrows. Keep a copy of the recorded deed and your closing statement with your tax records. The recorded copy is your proof that title moved, and you may want it later if the Trustee mails a bill to the wrong name.

Expect $12.00 for the first two pages and $5.00 for every added page or attachment. Transfer tax at 37 cents per hundred dollars of price, plus a $1.00 probate fee, is added to that.

Does the Sevier County Register of Deeds return my original?

Yes. The office sends originals back every time. If you mail the packet, include a self-addressed stamped envelope so the recorded copy reaches you quickly.

What is the Sevier County mortgage tax?

The rate is $0.115 per $100 of debt, with the first $2,000 exempt. The borrower pays at recording, and the mortgage or deed of trust has to state the maximum principal indebtedness.

How do I search Sevier County land records?

Click Search Land Records on the county's Register of Deeds page and look up by book and page. If an older instrument is hard to find, call 865.453.2758.

Can I be notified if someone files a document in my name?

Yes. Sign up for the Register's name alert and you will be told whenever a document is filed under your name or business, which helps you catch a bad filing early.

The office is at 155 N. Ocoee Street, Suite 102, Cleveland, TN 37311, and the phone number is 423-728-7240. Bradley County's July 2025 estimate is 115,465 residents and 47,861 housing units. Owners live in 67.3 percent of the homes. The median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $261,900 and median gross rent is $1,030, a number landlords can use to compare selling with holding. Cleveland is the county seat and largest city, and Charleston is the other city. Public schools are split between Bradley County Schools and Cleveland City Schools.

Ridges run through the county, and Candies Creek Ridge crosses Cleveland. A lot on a slope needs a careful survey and drainage check before a buyer's lender signs off.

Sellers here should keep the parcel number handy for the title company. It appears on the tax bill and goes on the deed.

Searching land records online

TitleSearcher is the vendor site the county recommends, and it offers online access to land records twenty-four hours a day. It holds images and index data for deeds, mortgages, releases, powers of attorney, restrictions, plat maps and other filings at the register's office.

There is also a property fraud alert sign-up linked from the register's page. It flags any new filing recorded in your name, which is useful for a rental, inherited land or a lot you rarely see. A forger working against an empty house is counting on the owner not noticing.

Ahead of listing, get your parcel's vesting deed and look at three things: how each owner name is spelled, the legal description, and whether an old deed of trust was left unreleased. A paid-off lender that never filed a release leaves a cloud on title, and the closing agent will want it cleared.

What recording a deed costs in tax

These taxes come from state law and do not vary by county. Tennessee charges $0.37 per $100 as a realty transfer tax and $0.115 per $100 of debt as a mortgage tax, leaving the first $2,000 of debt untaxed.

Exempt transfers

A short list of transfers is excluded by the state manual. Many of them arise in estates, divorces and family moves, when an owner may want to sell in a hurry.

  • An executor's deed fulfilling a devise in a will.
  • Divorce settlement decrees and deeds between the parties.
  • One spouse conveying to the other to start or end a tenancy by the entirety.
  • A person moving property into a revocable living trust they made, and moves back to that person or the spouse.
  • Property formerly held by tenants in common, and a life estate released to the remainder beneficiaries.
  • Deals with a government entity.

An exempt transfer needs no oath of consideration. With a taxable deed, the buyer swears to the price or value on the deed's face while the register watches, and the state may later set that number beside the assessor's value.

Stating value on the deed

Between unrelated parties, the price actually paid is normally what you state. When value is what sets the tax, the state treats the assessor's tax base, or an appraisal the assessor has accepted, as fair market value. Report less and you may face an audit, penalties and interest.

The Assessor of Property works from the Courthouse Annex at 155 Broad Street NW, Room 105; the phone is 423-728-7125. It also operates a Tennessee property viewer with parcel data and tax maps. State rules that affect your deed

Several Department of Revenue rules are applied at the register's counter, and a closing that knows them in advance will not stall over a technicality.

  • If one transfer of a tract produces several deeds, tax is paid a single time, and nothing is owed until title actually passes.
  • A modified or amended deed or deed of trust needs the earlier document's book and page, which shows the register that tax was already paid.
  • Any instrument showing debt must state the maximum principal indebtedness. The register cannot record it until the statement is given and the tax is paid.
  • When a buyer assumes a loan and the seller remains liable, no new debt exists and no mortgage tax is due. A new contract that releases the seller does create new debt, and it is taxed.
  • To prove tax was paid elsewhere, name the jurisdiction and give the book and page of the recorded document.

With a loan payoff, ask the lender how and when it will file the release of its deed of trust. That release clears the record, and the buyer's title agent will look for it.

Recording stays simple with a cash sale. We buy Bradley County houses as-is, and the deed goes onto the record here like any other. Without a lender there is no deed of trust and no mortgage tax, though the buyer still pays the transfer tax and swears to the value. The closing date is your call, and no loan approval holds things up.

Have the previous deed, your tax bill and any payoff figures on hand. If a deed contains an error, remember that the register records documents exactly as presented. The title company or attorney who drafted it can tell you how to fix it, and 423-728-7240 will confirm what the office needs to accept the corrected version.

Visit 155 N. Ocoee Street, Suite 102 in Cleveland, TN 37311, or call 423-728-7240.

Yes. TitleSearcher, the vendor the county points to, has land record images and index data all day and night, and the register's page links a property fraud alert sign-up.

It is $0.37 per $100 of price or value, and every Tennessee county charges the same. The buyer on the deed owes it, collected by the register at recording.

No. Mortgage tax is $0.115 per $100 of debt past the first $2,000 and applies to instruments like a deed of trust, and a cash purchase has none.

The register records what is presented. Ask whoever drafted the deed how to correct it, then call 423-728-7240 to learn what the office needs.

Go to room 400 of the Courthouse, 625 Georgia Avenue, Chattanooga, TN 37402. Doors are open Monday through Friday, eight to four, and shut on county holidays. The phone number is 423-209-6560.

By statute (Tenn. Code Ann. 66-24-101) the register records deeds and other instruments the law allows, then collects and accounts for the fees and taxes attached to them. Plats, powers of attorney, mortgages and military discharges all go through the same counter. When a Hamilton County house sells, the deed for that sale ends up here. Most sellers never need to visit. The title company or closing attorney carries the deed over, pays the fees and taxes, and files electronically if it uses one of the vendors listed below. If you do go yourself, bring the signed and notarized deed, a way to pay the filing fee and tax, and any exemption language your transfer relies on. Staff can answer questions about what the office will accept.

Recording a standard deed of two pages or fewer is $12.00, which includes a $2.00 data processing fee. Add $5.00 for every extra page. Taxes are billed in addition to filing fees.

Your title company usually adds these up for you and lists them on the settlement statement, but if you file yourself, bring a check large enough to cover the fee, the tax and the extras, and ask the counter to confirm the figure before you hand over the deed.

Transfer tax on a Hamilton County home sale

State realty transfer tax runs 37 cents per $100 of the tax base. It is the named grantee's bill, collected at filing by the register in the county where the deed is offered. Deeds of trust carry a mortgage tax of $0.115 per $100 after the first $2,000.

  • As a rule the base is whichever is higher, price paid or value.

Transfers exempt from transfer tax

Many family and estate transfers escape the tax, and the Department of Revenue's recordation tax help center names each. Staff at the register can tell you what exemption wording they expect on your deed.

If you record an affidavit of heirship, a correction affidavit or a similar paper before closing, have the notary read this notice first.

E-recording and searching land records

Electronic filers are pointed to two vendors. Simplifile answers at (800) 460-5657. Corporation Service Company is at (866) 652-0111 or eRecording.com. Ask your title company whether it submits that way.

Searching the database online is a separate step. You complete a print or online application, and the $50 fee, plus a monthly access fee, must be paid before passwords go out. The office also publishes an instructions PDF for the record search, a document requirement guide, a public records policy and request form, and a monthly report of the property transactions recorded the month before.

Need a single deed? Certified copies run $1.00 a page for deeds and $5.00 a page for plats. Call 423-209-6560 for questions about a specific instrument.

Property tax after the deed is recorded

From the register's pages you can reach three tools: the Assessor of Property, the Trustee's online property search, and Chattanooga's property tax site, where bills from both governments can be searched and paid. No registration is needed to look up a bill on the Chattanooga site.

If your house is in Chattanooga, expect both a county and a city bill. If it is in another part of the county, ask the Trustee which municipal bill, if any, applies. Have the title company run both searches before closing, so any unpaid tax comes out of your proceeds instead of following the house.

Hamilton County for sellers

The county spans 576 square miles of southeast Tennessee. Chattanooga is the seat, on the Tennessee River, with Georgia to the south. Collegedale, East Ridge, Lakesite, Red Bank, Ridgeside, Soddy-Daisy, Lookout Mountain, Signal Mountain and Walden are the other incorporated places.

How do I reach the Hamilton County register?

Who pays the transfer tax on a Hamilton County deed?

The books begin in 1854, when the county was re-established after earlier courts had dissolved it. Staff will talk you through a fee, but writing a deed is outside what they can do. On a typical sale a title company or attorney drafts the instrument, and the register files it after the tax is paid.

Deeds and trust deeds are priced per thousand dollars, with page, clerk and flat charges layered on. Anything filed electronically also carries a $2.00 fee, which began July 1, 2023.

A seller's biggest saving here is knowing the number early. Ask your title agent which side of the table the contract assigns each tax to, and confirm the figure used as the sale price matches the contract, since the oath and the tax follow from it.

Which party pays each line is a matter for the purchase contract and your title agent. Request a written estimate of both taxes and the recording charges ahead of closing, so the numbers on the settlement statement hold still.

  5. Once it is filed, request a copy of what was recorded and keep it with your closing papers.

When a buyer pays cash and takes the house as-is, the deed may be the only paper that reaches the register, so the visit goes quickly if everything is in order.

Can anyone request a copy of a recorded Putnam County deed?

Yes. All recorded documents are public except DD-214 discharge papers. Ask in person, by phone, by mail or by email.

At presentation, the buyer or the buyer's agent takes an oath on the stated value, in front of the register, and the oath appears on the face of the deed. A knowingly false figure is perjury. A signed contract sends the title company or attorney off to search for liens, draft the deed and arrange the oath of value. The seller signs the deed at closing, the buyer funds the transfer tax and any mortgage tax, and the register stamps the documents with a book and page number.

No tax is owed when you place a house in a revocable living trust that you or your spouse created, or when the trustee transfers it back. The deed still needs to meet the recording rules.

The state conveyance tax runs $3.70 on every $1,000 of value, the same as $0.37 per $100. The Register collects it under T.C.A. 67-4-409 at the time of recording. Add the $1.00 register's fee, plus the per-page charge and the $2.00 processing fee, and that is what a deed costs to record.

Loans are taxed separately at $1.15 per $1,000 of debt, with $2,000 left out of the calculation. That tax applies to the buyer's mortgage, not to the seller.

The statute exempts certain transfers, among them conveyances between spouses that create or end a tenancy by the entirety, deeds that carry out a will, moves into and out of a revocable living trust, and divorce settlement deeds. How do I file or search records in Robertson County?

You may hand a paper original over the counter or send the file electronically. Online records begin January 1, 1998, and the office points researchers to ustitlesearch.com.

  • Electronic recording: accepted through Simplifile, Corporation Service Company and ePN (eRecording Partners).
  • Paper filing: bring the original to the office during business hours along with payment.
  • Preparer details: state law requires a preparer's name and address on every document except releases and charters.
  • Drafting: a title company or lawyer should prepare the deed ahead of your visit.

For a full ownership history on an older parcel, a title company is the usual route. Online records cover only the years since the start date above, and anything earlier means asking staff or paying for a title search.

What the Assessor does after a deed is recorded

A copy of the recorded deed reaches the Assessor of Property the next day. Getting the buyer's name onto the parcel takes about 90 days, and in the meantime the next tax notice goes to whoever was on file for January 1.

Plan for that gap, because the current year's bill may still show your name after closing. The closing papers should spell out who pays for that year, and the address printed on the deed is what the Assessor uses for the following year's notice. The Assessor works at 521 S. Brown St. in Springfield, 615-384-4311. The Trustee, at 515 S. Brown St., 615-384-4238, supplies tax payoffs.

How the Register, Assessor and Trustee fit together in a sale

A sale passes through three desks in a fixed order. The Register gets the deed, the Assessor sees it a day later, and the Trustee collects any tax still owing.

  • Before closing: call the Trustee for the balance on each parcel you own, because deeds are indexed under varied spellings and a name search alone can miss one.
  • At closing: state tax and recording charges are collected by the Register, and any open tax is settled with the Trustee.
  • After closing: the Assessor updates the owner name, and the address on the deed drives next year's bill.

A bill that reaches one year delinquent moves to Robertson County Chancery Court, 615-384-5650, and a suit is filed for the tax. Ask the Trustee which stage your bill is in before choosing a closing day.

Springfield anchors the county, and Adams, Cedar Hill, Cross Plains, Greenbrier and Orlinda also record through the same Register.

Guarding against deed fraud

The Register promotes My Land Alert, a service with free monitoring and notification, no contract and email privacy. Sign up at mylandalert.com to get a message when a document is recorded against your name.

Keep the recorded copy of your deed with your closing papers so you can match the instrument number the Register assigned. If an alert ever arrives for a document you do not recognize, call the office right away and bring that instrument number with you.

A seller's checklist for recording

Recording goes fast when the paperwork is ready. Ahead of closing day, run down this list.

  1. Learn who is preparing the deed and whether it will be filed electronically or on paper.
  2. Confirm the preparer's name and address appear on the deed.
  3. Check that any lender being paid off has sent its release, so title reads clean.
  4. Get the Trustee's payoff for every parcel in your name.
  5. Keep the recorded copy afterward, with the instrument number the office assigns.

Even a cash buyer who takes the house as-is needs the deed recorded, so none of these steps drop away.

What is the minimum Robertson County deed recording fee?

$12.00 before tax: a $10.00 minimum charge plus the $2.00 processing fee. Longer deeds pay $5.00 per page, and a $1.00 register's fee is added when state tax is collected.

What is the Robertson County deed tax rate?

The state conveyance tax is $3.70 per $1,000 of value. Mortgages are taxed at $1.15 per $1,000 once the first $2,000 is set aside.

Does the Robertson County Register accept electronic filings?

Yes. Simplifile, Corporation Service Company and eRecording Partners are listed. Paper originals are accepted at the counter during business hours.

How far back do Robertson County online deed records go?

Internet records begin January 1, 1998, searchable through ustitlesearch.com. For anything earlier, ask the Register's staff.

How long until a buyer appears on the Robertson County tax rolls?

About 90 days after the Assessor gets the recorded deed copy, which arrives the day after recording. The bill goes to the January 1 name until the next year.

Where deeds are recorded

To record a Williamson County deed, go to Suite 201 at 1320 West Main Street in Franklin, TN 37064, home of the Register of Deeds. Mail can be addressed to P. O. Box 808, Franklin, TN 37065. Call 615-790-5706 or write to register@williamsoncounty-tn.gov. The counter is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM.

The public file of deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, plats, liens, judgments and wills lives here, a duty the office ties to T.C.A. 66-24-101. Anything never recorded cannot be found by a title searcher, so do not skip this step on a quick sale.

The same building houses the County Clerk (Suite 135), the Trustee (Suite 203) and the Property Assessor (Suite 300). One trip can cover both a records question and a tax question.

Market context for sellers

Roughly 584 square miles of Middle Tennessee make up this county, and Franklin is both seat and biggest city. Brentwood, Fairview, Spring Hill (partly in Maury County), Nolensville and Thompson's Station are also here. Residents numbered 247,726 in 2020 and about 272,061 by the 2025 estimate, against 183,182 in 2010. Owners occupy 78.5% of occupied homes among the 91,133 housing units counted then. Williamson County Schools operates 50 schools, and one slice of Franklin falls under the Franklin Special School District for K to 8. After years of steady growth, most sales here pair the release of an old deed of trust with a new one, both handled by this office.

Recordation taxes on a deed

Two state taxes attach to recording. Staff collect them at filing and pass them on to the Department of Revenue. Realty transfer tax is the buyer's (grantee's) cost when real property changes hands. The indebtedness tax applies to a recorded deed of trust or mortgage.

Recordation taxes collected at filing
TaxRateApplies to
Realty transfer tax37 cents per $100, generally on the greater of price paid or property valueDeeds and other transfer instruments
Indebtedness (mortgage) tax$0.115 per $100 of debt, after the first $2,000Deeds of trust, mortgages, financing statements

Exact amounts for your sale appear on the settlement statement. The statute behind both, Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409, ties them to the instrument, so payment comes before recording.

Recording fees

The office runs a fee calculator inside its ProAccess system. Pick the instrument type, enter the page count, and the screen breaks out a recording fee, a register's fee, a DP fee and an archive fee, then gives the total due. Run it rather than estimate, because every added page moves the total.

The menu includes deed, quitclaim deed, trustee's deed, installment deed, deed of trust, release, plat, easement, lis pendens, power of attorney and last will and testament. Home sales usually involve just three: the warranty or quitclaim deed, a release of the seller's existing deed of trust, and the buyer's lender paperwork.

County or state changes can alter the fees for an instrument, so run the calculator on the day you file. If your document type is unusual, ask staff at 615-790-5706.

Filing happens at the Franklin counter or online through an e-recording partner. Four services are approved:

Lenders and title companies normally use these channels. If you are selling privately, carry the signed, notarized deed to the counter and pay the fees and transfer tax there.

Also available: a fraud alert subscription, TitleSearcher for searching records, and Pro Access for professional account holders. A name search on those tools before listing shows whether anyone has recorded something against your parcel.

A release of trust deed removes your old mortgage from the record after payoff. Property taxes at a sale

Statements are mailed in early October, and payment is open from the first Monday that month until February 28 the next year, with partial payments allowed. From March 1, 1.5% interest accrues, repeating on the first of each later month, and the Trustee has no power to waive, prorate or release it.

A tax year is January 1 to December 31, and the owner of record on January 1 receives the bill. When you sell, hand it to the buyer; the contract or the title company decides what each side pays at closing. The Trustee is in Suite 203, phone 615-790-5709, and the Assessor takes value questions at 615-790-5708.

Owe something? Ask the Trustee for the exact balance before the contract date. The closing agent can then settle it from your sale proceeds.

Before the deed is recorded

Most delays come from a handful of misses. Run this list with your closing agent.

  • Order a title search so liens and old deeds of trust turn up early.
  • Confirm the Trustee shows no balance on the parcel for the current tax year.
  • Have every signature notarized with the notary block fully completed.
  • Run the fee calculator with the real page count so the check or wire is right.
  • Decide whether the closing will be filed in person or through one of the four e-recording partners.

In order, a typical sale goes like this. The title search finds any old deed of trust. The seller signs the deed before a notary. The closing agent totals the fees and the transfer tax. The documents are then filed at the counter or sent through an e-recording partner, and the old mortgage is released once the lender is paid. Ask your agent which step each document is waiting on if recording seems slow.

After recording, the office stamps the document with its book and page. Keep that copy in your closing file, since lenders and buyers request it years on. A cash sale may have no new deed of trust to record, yet the deed and its transfer tax still go through this office.

Frequently asked questions

Who pays the transfer tax?

It is charged to the buyer as grantee, at 37 cents per $100, usually on whichever is higher, the price or the value. Contracts can move that cost, so check yours.

What are the office hours?

The counter is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM at 1320 West Main Street, Suite 201, Franklin. Call 615-790-5706 to check holiday hours. E-recording partners accept submissions outside counter hours.

Can I record a deed without a title company?

Yes. Take the signed, notarized deed to the counter with the calculator total and the transfer tax. Searching title first still pays off because liens would follow the property.

Does the Register of Deeds collect property taxes?

No. Property taxes go to the Trustee in Suite 203 of the same building, phone 615-790-5709. The Register collects only recordation taxes and recording fees.

What happens to my tax bill if I sell?

The bill goes to the owner of record on January 1, so you pass it to the buyer. The Trustee will not prorate or waive interest, so the contract and closing statement decide the split. Ask for the balance before closing.

This is where the public record of who owns what is kept, along with liens and contracts. Transfer tax by deed type

Tennessee's realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100. The buyer pays at recording, and the amount is measured differently for each kind of deed.

Deed typeTax base
Warranty deed or other freehold transferWhichever is greater, the consideration or the property's value at transfer
Quitclaim deedThe consideration given, unless the deed's wording shows the grantor meant to convey the property itself
Warranty deed with a retained life estateFair market value less the value of the life estate
Modified or amended deedMust cite the earlier deed's book and page, proving the original tax was paid

Wording such as "to have and to hold" or "in fee simple" may move a quitclaim deed to the fair market value basis. If a seller keeps a life estate, the preparer values that estate and subtracts it, which shrinks the base. Your closing attorney handles that calculation. The oath of value

Someone on the buying side, whether the buyer, an agent or a trustee, takes an oath at the register's counter. They state the actual consideration or the property's value, whichever is larger, and the statement goes on the face of the deed. If a transfer is exempt, the oath is skipped. Knowingly stating a false figure can lead to a perjury charge.

For fair market value the state looks to the tax base on file at the assessor's office, and it will also take a recent appraisal that office has accepted. Reporting less than that opens the door to an audit plus penalties and interest. Reviewers pick counties at random, pull recorded deeds, compare the sworn number with the assessor value on the Comptroller's website, and may send the person named on the deed an inquiry letter.

No one pays twice for one transaction. If several deeds cover a single transfer of one parcel, the tax is paid once, and nothing is owed until title really passes by deed.

A deed of trust triggers a mortgage tax, separate from the transfer tax, of $0.115 per $100 of debt with $2,000 excluded. The borrower pays, and the register holds the instrument until payment is made. Loan assumptions are treated their own way. Suppose a buyer takes over your loan. If you stay liable on the old debt, no new tax applies. If the buyer signs a fresh agreement with the lender and your obligation is cancelled, the new mortgage is taxed. Mechanics, contractor, subcontractor and laborer liens and judgment liens are not subject to the mortgage tax. They can still hang over the title, so have the title company search for them well ahead of closing.

With a sale pending, ask the trustee where the account stands. Any unpaid balance is subtracted from your proceeds at closing. Get the figure early and pass it along to the title company.

Some owners pick a cash sale to dodge repairs, showings and the wait for a buyer's financing. We buy Bedford County houses as-is. Yes. Sign up for the register's free fraud alert and you will be notified of transfers filed under your name. Several name variations can be enrolled.

The assessor's counter opens at eight and closes at half past four, Monday through Friday. A record card exists for each of the roughly 25,000 parcels countywide. The cards are refreshed weekly through the state's Local Assessor System for web viewing, and a public terminal at the office can pull them up. Staff can read you the owner of record and the classification, which is worth hearing before you pick a list price.

Transfer tax on a Franklin County sale

Tennessee collects 37 cents per $100 of the price or value whenever real property changes hands. The buyer hands it to the register when the deed is recorded. The larger of the price paid or the property's value is the base, and the buyer swears to that figure in front of the register.

New loans also carry a mortgage tax of 11.5 cents per $100 of debt past the first $2,000, paid by the borrower.

A deed that cites a statutory exemption skips the oath. Among the exempt transfers are ending a tenancy by the entirety and releasing a life estate to the beneficiaries. If yours might fit, tell the person drafting the deed before it reaches the counter.

Why the register might refuse a deed

The register checks whether a paper can be accepted and leaves its legal effect to the drafter. County advisers at the University of Tennessee list the requirements below.

  • Readable text and a notary's acknowledgment (Tennessee Code sections 66-24-101 and 66-22-101)
  • Names and addresses of the owner and the taxpayer, section 66-24-114
  • A derivation clause that cites the prior deed, section 66-24-110
  • The drafter's name and address, section 66-24-115
  • The parcel number, section 66-24-122
  • Fees, plus transfer tax if any is owed, on the day of filing

A document in another language needs a translation attached, and registers may turn away an unreadable page. One missing item sends the deed back, which can push a closing date. Match the deed's parcel number to your tax bill before signing.

What happens at the counter

Whoever carries your deed to the register hands over the original, the fees and, where tax is owed, the transfer tax. Staff check the paper against the list above. If it passes, it is indexed in the county seat and becomes part of the public record of who owns the land.

Expect a few practical limits. Staff do not draft or fix a deed for you, and they will not say whether a document does what you intend. If the preparer left off a required item, the deed goes back and the closing may slip until it is corrected. That is why sellers do well to ask the title company to review the deed before signing day, and why a clean parcel number matters.

Wills, court orders, leases and military discharges are kept in the same record system as deeds. So the office is also the place to look if you inherited a house and need to see what has been filed against it.

Local market snapshot

Franklin County sits on the Alabama line in the eastern part of Middle Tennessee, with Winchester as the seat. About 45,579 people live here, up 6.6 percent from 2020. Roughly 77.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Median home value sits at $236,900 and median gross rent at $894. Builders pulled 323 permits in 2025. Communities named on the county site are Cowan, Decherd, Estill Springs, Sewanee, Huntland, Sherwood and Winchester, and Interstate 24 connects the county to Chattanooga.

Property tax calendar

The assessment date is January 1. Payment opens the first Monday in October and stays interest-free through February 28. Balances are delinquent from March 1.

State law makes the assessor responsible for locating and identifying every taxable property in the county, appraising it and setting its assessed value. The trustee only bills and collects, so take a value complaint to the assessor before anyone else. The commission sets the rate. Homes are assessed at a quarter of appraised value. Divide that assessed value by 100 and multiply by the rate to get the tax. The trustee can quote the current rate and your balance.

Formal challenges start at the county board of equalization, which convenes June 1. State relief may be open to older or disabled owners whose 2025 income was $38,470 or less. The trustee takes the form, and it is due within 35 days after the delinquency date.

What to do before you sell

Begin at the assessor's counter. Request your parcel's record card and compare owner name, parcel number and classification with your deed, because errors are simpler to correct before a title company finds them. Then phone the trustee at (931) 967-2962 and ask what is owed on the parcel.

Once a closing date exists, find out who will carry the deed to Winchester, the title company or an attorney. Confirm that the release of your old loan will be recorded too. After recording, the register's office can tell you whether both papers are indexed. A cash buyer often closes quickly, and the same recording steps apply with no lender paperwork in the way.

Bring a short list when you visit the courthouse: your deed, your latest tax bill and a note of any liens you expect to be released. The assessor's public terminal lets you look up the same web records a buyer's agent will see, and those records update weekly, so a correction you request now should show up before your listing goes live. Three offices share one building, which keeps the whole round of checks to a single trip.

At the Register of Deeds, 1 South Jefferson Street, Winchester, TN 37398. The phone number is (931) 967-2840.

Who do I call to check my Franklin County property tax?

Call the Franklin County Trustee at (931) 967-2962. The trustee collects the tax, while the Property Assessor at (931) 967-3869 handles the appraisal and assessment.

How many parcels does the Franklin County assessor track?

About 25,000. Every parcel has a record card, and the data refreshes weekly for web viewing through the state's Local Assessor System.

What transfer tax applies when a Franklin County house sells?

37 cents per $100 of the price or value, paid by the buyer at recording.

What does a Franklin County deed need to be accepted?

It needs readable text, a notary acknowledgment, owner and taxpayer addresses, a reference to the prior deed, the drafter's details, a parcel number and fees. If one is missing, the register returns the deed.

What this office records

A sale turns public at this counter. The deed for a Morristown house is handed in, given a book and page reference, and added to the chain of title that future buyers, lenders and title searchers will read. Staff also record deeds of trust, releases of paid-off loans, powers of attorney, charters, plats and military discharges.

Records on file go back to 1860. Deeds and plats from 1978 forward are being scanned into digital form, so ask staff how to search for anything older.

Two state taxes pass through the counter as well: the realty transfer tax on land sales and the mortgage tax on debt. Every register must collect them for the Tennessee Department of Revenue, and on a typical sale they come to far more than the filing fee.

Office location and what to bring

Find the register on the third floor of the Administrative Building, part of the courthouse complex at 511 West Second North Street, Morristown, TN 37814. Call 423-586-6551, or fax 423-318-2505.

Pack a short list before you go:

  • The signed deed, plus the buyer or an agent ready to swear to the price or value before the register
  • Parcel details from the assessor, who works in the same building on 423-586-1852
  • If the deed corrects an earlier one, the book and page of the version already recorded
  • Funds for the filing fee and the tax

Hamblen County has 68,843 residents in 28,945 housing units. Home values center on $210,900, and 258 new-construction permits were issued in 2025.

Before closing day, ask your title company whether it will present the deed in person or send it, and confirm who will bring the funds for the filing fee and tax. If you are handling the paperwork yourself, call the register's number first to check what the counter needs for your particular document.

Filing charges

Tennessee sets recording fees by statute, so every county charges the same amounts. The list below follows the University of Tennessee county assistance service's summary of a register's standard fees. Military discharges are filed at no charge.

What the buyer owes at recording

Tennessee's realty transfer tax runs 37 cents for every $100 of price, or 0.37 percent. Revenue officials apply it to the larger of the price paid or the parcel's worth on the transfer date. The grantee is the responsible party under state law, and payment goes to the register where the deed is presented. How the cost is shared between buyer and seller appears on your closing statement.

Each deed needs a sworn statement of the real consideration or value, taken in front of the register. Lying on it is perjury. If a buyer holds several deeds to one parcel, the tax is paid once. Nothing is owed until title truly passes by deed.

From time to time the state pulls recorded deeds and compares the sworn value with the assessor's number, and a gap can trigger a letter. As proof of value, the state takes the assessor's tax base or a recent appraisal the assessor's office has accepted.

Transfers that owe no transfer tax

The Revenue Department's manual lists these among the transfers that escape the tax:

  • Conveyances between spouses, or ones that create or end an entireties tenancy
  • A deed an executor signs to carry out a will
  • Transfers made under a divorce decree or domestic settlement
  • A home placed in a revocable living trust by its creator or the creator's spouse, and taken back out
  • Distributions by a trustee to beneficiaries under a will or revocable trust
  • Transfers to or from a government body

An exempt transfer needs no oath. Quitclaim deeds get a closer look from the state. Here tax follows the consideration given, except when the wording shows intent to convey the property itself. Phrases such as to have and to hold or in fee simple do that, and market value then controls.

Mortgage tax on new loans

Recording a deed of trust or similar debt instrument triggers an indebtedness tax of $0.115 per $100 of debt, with the first $2,000 exempt. The borrower settles it at the register together with the filing charges.

Somewhere on the instrument, or in a sworn attachment, the maximum principal indebtedness must be stated for Tennessee recording tax purposes. Without that statement and payment, the register cannot record it. Skipping or shorting the tax brings a penalty of $250 or twice the unpaid amount, whichever is more.

Loan assumptions fall into two groups. If the buyer merely agrees to pay the seller's debt and the seller stays liable, nothing new is taxed, since the debt already existed. When the buyer signs a fresh contract with the lender that cancels the seller's duty, the new mortgage carries the tax.

For a seller, the practical point is simple. If your buyer finances, the lender's deed of trust is recorded along with your deed, and the buyer's closing costs include this tax. If your buyer pays cash, there is no new mortgage to record, so only the transfer tax and filing charges apply. Either way, the title company should show every recording charge on the settlement statement before you sign.

How to research a deed or parcel

The Assessor of Property is the best first stop, and that office is in the same courthouse. The assessor's office keeps ownership, address, deed references and appraised value for roughly 32,000 parcels and maintains more than 400 maps showing lot lines and acreage. Take the book and page number from that record to the register to read the recorded instrument itself.

Certified copies cost $1 a page. The scanning project covers 1978 forward, so ask staff how to search for earlier records.

Planning to sell fast? Ask the title company to pull the chain of title at the start. Three problems stall closings: a deed never recorded, a release missing on an old loan, and a name on the deed that differs from the tax roll.

When you inherit a house, the register is also where you can see which instruments are on file against it, such as a deed of trust that was never released. Staff can point you to the right book and page, though they will not interpret a document for you.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Hamblen County register's office?

Third floor, Administrative Building, 511 West Second North Street in Morristown. The phone is 423-586-6551.

What does it cost to file a deed in Hamblen County?

The first two pages cost ten dollars, each added page is $5, and there are $2 for data processing and $1 for the tax receipt. Transfer tax at $0.37 per $100 is separate.

Which party is responsible for transfer tax on a Hamblen County sale?

The grantee is legally responsible and pays when the deed is filed. Your closing statement shows how buyer and seller handled the cost.

Do any Hamblen County deeds skip the transfer tax?

Yes. Spousal transfers, an executor's deed, divorce decree transfers and trust moves are some of those exempt.

Does the Register of Deeds keep property tax records?

No. The Assessor of Property, 423-586-1852, holds values and tax rolls, and the Trustee, 423-586-6290, takes payment. The register records deeds and gathers the state recording taxes.

Preparing for a Tipton County closing

A sale involves a few offices in a set order. First confirm the tax status with the Trustee, then have the title company or attorney prepare the deed. The signed deed, with the fees and state tax, goes to the Register, and the recorded deed then feeds the Assessor's records. If the buyer borrows, the lender's mortgage or deed of trust is recorded alongside it and a payoff release for your old loan follows.

Close to a sale, ask three things. Who is delivering the documents to Covington? Which party covers the transfer tax under the contract? Does the parcel carry a city bill as well as a county bill? A cash sale leaves out the lender's paperwork and the mortgage tax, so the recording packet is shorter and the fees are mostly the deed charges above. Keep the recorded deed with your closing papers for later reference.

Bring or send the originals only. Copies are not a substitute for the signed deed, and a deed missing a page can hold up the whole filing. If a certified copy of an older deed is needed for the sale, the Register charges $1.00 per page, so ask for it a few days before closing rather than the day of. Plats cost $15.00 to record, which applies mostly to new subdivisions and not to a resale of an existing house.

Frequently asked questions

Which office accepts a deed for recording in Tipton County?

The Register of Deeds in Covington. The office mails to PO Box 626, Covington, TN 38019, and answers deed questions at 901-476-0204.

What fees apply when a Tipton County deed is recorded?

The base charge is $10.00 for up to two pages, with $5.00 for every page beyond that, a $2.00 data processing fee, and a $1.00 clerk's fee whenever state tax is paid.

How big is the state tax on a Tipton County sale?

The state charges $0.37 for each $100 of the price. Your title company can work out the exact figure for your sale.

Does a Tipton County loan carry its own tax?

Yes. The state mortgage tax is $0.115 for each $100 of debt beyond the first $2,000.

Is there a free warning when something is filed under my name?

Yes. The Register sponsors a free fraud alert at mylandalert.com. Once you enroll a name, an email arrives each time a document is filed under it.
